column6: Fine-medium hair sits above the headline; she self-selects by hair type before she reads a benefit.
Her name printed on the bottle is the product; personalisation is being sold as being seen.
Replaced every other one I owned is a clear-out, not a purchase; the two litre bottles are the commitment.
If you've ever straightened your textured hair is an accusation she recognises as her own history.
The ad puts her objection in the headline and then answers it in eight lines; she will read all of them.
A diagram instead of a claim; she wants to see how the formula was decided before she trusts it.
A man who looks like he does not think about his hair, talking about his hair; that contradiction is the permission.
A mic and a cap; the podcast staging tells him this is a conversation he is overhearing.
Ocean-inspired waves is a look she can name; healthier is the excuse that lets her buy it.
Stiff is the word for the gel he is leaving; natural texture is what he thinks he is allowed to want now.
Easy hair routine is the whole promise; he is buying fewer steps, not better hair.
Flannel in a barn selling styling product; the setting is doing the work of saying this is still masculine.
Forty-five cents a day converts a tin into a subscription he can justify without thinking about the tin.
No claim, just hair being touched; the shot is the outcome and the brand is trusting her to want it.
Oily roots, flakes and congested scalp listed as questions; she answers yes to at least one and stays.
Your guide and step by step; she needs to be taught the routine before she will buy the bottle.
Parting her own hair to show the scalp; the inspection is the format and the flakes are the subject.
In one wash sets the horizon; she will not persist with something that takes a month to prove itself.
Beauty editors is the shortcut; she outsources the shortlist to people paid to try everything.
Two full-size bottles held up like a haul; the size signals she has already been through one.
